key_insight: LLM-assisted filtering of potentially unreliable training labels improved EEG sleep-stage classification without adding an LLM at inference.
clinical_relevance: The approach may support lightweight wearable sleep monitoring, but clinical utility remains unestablished.
method: Train TinySleepNet and flag low-confidence EEG epochs.
Use LLaMA 3.1 to assess flagged labels against AASM guidelines using spectral features and sequence context.
Remove epochs judged suspicious and retrain TinySleepNet.
evidence_signal: On Sleep-EDF Expanded with 20-fold cross-validation, accuracy rose from 81.8% to 84.6% and macro F1 from 75.6% to 77.4%, with notable REM detection gains.
watch_item: Filtering may discard difficult but valid examples; independent validation of LLM judgments and performance is needed.
paper_title: LLM-Assisted Label Noise Correction for EEG-Based Sleep Stage Classification
